business_scope.primary_industry_name: Integration of Programmable Logic Controllers for Industrial Grids

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national legal system based on written codes and doctrinal case law)

France-United States Double Taxation Convention on Income and Capital (1967, amended by 2006 and 2013 protocols; separate Estate and Gift Tax Convention of 1978)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-2-2, L. 561-2-3 and R. 561-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier (UBO register obligations), implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Loi n° 2020-102 du 12 février 2020; Décret n° 2023-213 organizing the INPI Guichet unique UBO declaration; register access further restricted per the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 in Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 (WM v Sovim) and CNIL GDPR constraints.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (procuration) for the founder signing the statuts of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the founder's home jurisdiction or a French notaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille affixed by the competent authority of the issuing state (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each individual UBO and of the first statutory president
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille affixed to the certified true copy (or consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and registry extract of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Declaration of solvency and non-bankruptcy of each statutory director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction court registry, notary or equivalent competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation (traduction assermentée) of the complete apostilled documentary bundle
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-appointed certified translator (traducteur agréé) registered with a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translation certificate attached to the apostilled originals; no additional legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs and directors against the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council resolutions, OFAC SDN list, and French asset-freezing orders issued by the Ministère de l'Économie; mandatory PEP detection per FATF criteria and Article L. 561-10 of the Code monétaire et financier; screening is refreshed at the moment of filing with the INPI Guichet unique and again before the RCS registration is completed. For the low-risk ISIC 4321 tier, standard due diligence applies without automatic enhanced measures; a Tracfin suspicious-transaction report under Article L. 561-15 is triggered only where the wire-funding source or the intermediary ownership structure cannot be fully documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises de l'INPI at https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, the single electronic gateway replacing the former Centre de Formalités des Entreprises; the resulting inscription is recorded in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) held by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A registered company name may be in any language but must be expressible in Latin characters; any non-Latin script must be transliterated into a single Latin-character version and filed together with a French-language designatory phrase. Screening applies the principles of distinctiveness and verisimilitude under Articles R. 123-37 and R. 123-38 of the Code de commerce, and the name must not falsely imply a legal form different from the SAS (tokens such as SA, SARL, EURL, SE are screened out).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may within one month (i) obtain written grounds from the Greffe through the Guichet unique; (ii) file a reasoned administrative request for reconsideration with the greffier; and (iii) if the refusal is maintained, apply by assignation to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce (juge délégué) under Articles L. 123-1, R. 123-30 and R. 123-31 of the Code de commerce for an order compelling the greffier to complete the registration. Where the refusal is based on prior trademark rights, the parallel remedy is an opposition before the INPI or an action for nullification before the Tribunal Judiciaire under Article L. 711-4 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for the siège social: commercial domiciliation at a licensed business center is allowed for up to six renewable years under Articles L. 123-11-1 and R. 123-137 of the Code de commerce, and is regularly used by SAS founders. For the ISIC 4321 SCADA and PLC integration industry, a virtual address cannot substitute for operational substance (mobile technical crews, grid equipment storage, tooling and engineering management premises), because the DGFiP may re-characterize the actual place of business for VAT and corporate residence purposes; the registered-office address must remain a genuine administrative seat with mail, legal-notice and records reception capacity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximate annual probability of 7% to 12% of an unannounced on-site inspection (URSSAF control, DGFiP fiscal verification or labor inspectorate visit) within the first three accounting years for a standard-risk, low-tier entity with a verifiable operational base; the probability rises to 30% to 40% where the declared registered office provides the only commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of the French-language SAS statuts by a Paris-seated avocat, including the UBO annex schedule and corporate governance provisions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (approximately EUR 1,800 to EUR 2,600 fixed or on a lump-sum basis)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory auditor's report on non-cash contributions (rapport du commissaire aux apports), conditionally mandatory where in-kind contributions exceed EUR 30,000 in value or exceed one-half of the share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commissaire aux comptes (statutory auditor appointed for contribution valuation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory assignment with prevailing market benchmark of approximately EUR 800 to EUR 1,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation agreement with a licensed business center (year one, renewable up to six years)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation company (accredited business center in the Paris region)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of approximately EUR 240 to EUR 480 per year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague apostille and/or consular legalization of the foreign founders' identity, corporate, and solvency documentary bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French notaire and the diplomatic/consular authority of each document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff table plus consular fee schedule (approximately EUR 180 to EUR 350 for the bundle)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation (traduction assermentée) of the apostilled foreign documents by a court-appointed translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-appointed certified translator (traducteur agréé auprès de la Cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court tariff scale and market benchmark of approximately EUR 45 to EUR 60 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank certificate of deposit of the share capital (attestation de dépôt de capital) issued at the opening of the blocked capital account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank holding the capital blockage (or a notaire via Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated banking service fee of approximately EUR 120 to EUR 250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the statutory incorporation notice in a Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved for the registered-office jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory regulated tariff per insertion line (approximately EUR 160 to EUR 210)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic filing with the INPI Guichet unique, UBO declaration, and RCS registration at the commercial court registry (including greffe fees)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory public fee schedule (approximately EUR 25 to EUR 90 for the incorporation file)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title V — Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general formation rules under Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; regulatory provisions on RCS registration under Articles R.123-1 et seq. and R.227-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office department; electronic filing centralized through the Guichet Unique of the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and the single electronic incorporation form (Formulaire M0) filed with the RCS, culminating in the K-bis extract (certificate of incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS under the Code de commerce; the capital is freely set in the articles and must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account with a bank authorized by the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or with a notary, and at least 50% of cash subscriptions must be paid up upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. In-kind contributions are fully paid up upon delivery, and if they consist of real estate or going concern, require the intervention of a notary and a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the shareholders of [Company] (the 'Company'), upon incorporation, as follows: First, the subscription by the Shareholder(s) of [X] ordinary shares, each of a par value of €1, is hereby accepted and ratified. Second, the registered office of the Company is fixed at [Address], France; the Chairman is authorized to take any lease or other steps to render the office operational. Third, [Name] is appointed Chairman (Président) and [Name] is appointed General Manager (Directeur Général) for the duration of the corporate term. Fourth, the bank account mandate is granted accordingly. Fifth, the Chairman shall accomplish all formalities incidental to incorporation and the publication of the Company's existence; these resolutions take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, execution and notarization (if required) of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating shareholders acting through the Guichet Unique portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); notaire (mandatory only for contributions of real property or French registered going concern)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SAS articles in French, specifying the corporate name, corporate purpose (integration of programmable logic controllers and SCADA automation for electrical substations), registered office, share capital and classes of shares, transfer-of-shares rules, chairman and general-management powers, corporate term, and thresholds for statutory auditors. Ensure all shareholders sign the statuts; service contracts and leases can be signed after. Upload the final text to the Guichet Unique once signed.
required_dossiers: Statuts (Articles of Association) signed by all shareholders
Valid identity document (passport or national ID) of each shareholder
Declaration of the actual address (email and legal address) of the legal representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the articles as incomplete or contrary to Articles L.227-1 et seq., amend the text and have all shareholders re-sign; if notarization is made mandatory by the contributions, obtain the notarial deed before lodging the file; material defects may be regularized without nullity where the conditions of Article L.235-1 of the Commercial Code are satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of the subscribed share capital in an escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Credit institution authorized by the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) or a notary, acting as depositary of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The SAS in formation opens a non-interest-bearing 'capital deposit' account in the company's name. Transfer the amount of cash subscriptions due at incorporation (at least 50% of the nominal value, or the whole amount if preferred), identifying each subscriber. The depositary institution or notary issues the capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) certifying that the funds are blocked until the RCS registration. If the company is never registered, funds are returned to the subscribers.
required_dossiers: Statement of subscription of shares signed by each subscriber
Articles of Association and schedule of capital contributions
Valuation report of the commissaire aux apports (only when in-kind contributions are made)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary refuses (e.g., AML/KYC doubts), present additional origin-of-funds documentation or choose another CDC-approved bank; if the in-kind valuation is challenged, the shareholders may obtain a second appraisal and, failing agreement, apply to the President of the Commercial Court for the appointment of an independent expert.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal notice in an authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any newspaper authorized to publish legal announcements in the department of the registered office (Journal d'Annonces Légales — JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the mandatory notice stating the corporate name, legal form (SAS), share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, the date of signature of the articles, and the RCS registry of the registered office. Forward the notice to the chosen JAL; obtain the certificate of publication (certificat de parution) to be attached to the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Completed legal notice text (avis de constitution)
Power of attorney to the JAL agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice, correct the wording to match the articles and republish; the publication takes effect on the first publication date, which can be accelerated by selecting a daily gazette; if the certificate is delayed, contact the editor for a certified duplicate before the registration deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Single electronic filing with the RCS via the Guichet Unique (INPI portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); the file is electronically routed to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to www.formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, complete the corporate formation application (equivalent of the M0 form) using the company details prepared in Step 1, attach the statuts, the capital deposit certificate, the JAL publication certificate, the declaration of beneficial owners, and the proof of the registered office address. Pay the official greffe fee and any applicable duties by electronic payment. Track the file; the registry examines the file and issues the registration acceptance notice visible in the Guichet Unique dashboard.
required_dossiers: Application for registration (Formulaire M0) completed online
Signed and certified copy of the Articles of Association
Capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Declaration of beneficial owners (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Certificate of legal publication delivered by the JAL
Proof of the right to use the registered office (lease, free occupancy consent, or title)
Statement of the actual residence and the identity of the Chairman and corporate officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry must notify any deficiency through the Guichet Unique; the applicant has the statutory cure period to resubmit the missing or corrected items; if the cure period lapses, the file is closed and the incorporation must be resubmitted as a new application with a fresh M0; a refusal may be referred to the president of the competent commercial court for judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of the K-bis extract, release of capital and opening of the final bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry Clerk) and the depositary bank or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the verification, the greffe issues the K-bis extract (certificate of incorporation) evidencing the company's legal personality and the SIREN identification number. The registry notification to the depositary (or the notary) triggers the release of the blocked funds into the company's operating bank account. The K-bis must be kept in the corporate books and used to prove corporate capacity in commercial relations.
required_dossiers: Acceptance notice issued by the Greffe on the Guichet Unique
Receipt of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed beyond the statutory turnaround, contact the greffe and, if needed, escalate to the supervisory judge (juge commissaire) of the tribunal; if the K-bis contains errors, request a reasoned rectification application from the greffe, which must issue a corrected extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration registrations with INSEE, tax authorities and social administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques (INSEE); Direction Départementale des Finances Publiques (DDFIP); URSSAF and the statutory obligations of the company's officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The greffe automatically transmits the incorporation data to INSEE for SIREN/SIRET attribution and to the commercial court statistical agencies. The company should nevertheless verify that its VAT file is activated through the impots.gouv business portal and inform the tax service of first taxable transactions; the company must also register as an employer with URSSAF and file social declarations for any remunerated chairman and employees in accordance with the general social security scheme.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
Articles of Association (extract) with the appointment of officers
Identity and personal details of the Chairman and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SIREN/SIRET is not attributed within two weeks, apply to INSEE via the Guichet Unique for a duplicate registration; if VAT activation is missing, request an effective date of liability through the DDFIP; if URSSAF does not open the employer account, contact the URSSAF branch to correct the registration, providing the K-bis as proof of incorporation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no national industrial operation permit is required for a SCADA/PLC integration contractor under French law; the company should nonetheless hold a professional electrical qualification certificate (e.g., Qualifelec or OPQIBI) to evidence technical competence for infrastructure works by grid operators such as RTE or Enedis.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for the SCADA integration service activity itself; where the company performs fixed electrical installation works in substations, the works contract will require evidence of professional qualification and compliance with NF C 15-100 standards, rather than a separate operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) — Inspecteur des installations classées, under the Ministry of Ecological Transition
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — SCADA/PLC integration and electrical installation contracting are not inscribed in the ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) nomenclature; a Registration (Déclaration) under the ICPE regime would only become mandatory if the company's service workshop stored batteries, switchgear gas or other listed substances beyond the regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by the SCADA integration service; if the workshop handles WEEE, batteries or SF6-containing equipment, the waste shall be handed over exclusively to approved waste-treatment operators in compliance with Articles R.543-1 et seq. of the French Environmental Code; any refrigerant and solvent use is subject to the registration thresholds of the Technical Regulation applicable to the site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the registered office/workshop (attestation délivrée par un bureau de contrôle under Article R.123-43 of the French Construction and Housing Code for premises receiving employees); structural load inspection of any equipment storage area; electrical safety verification of the workshop installation by a qualified electrician; the employer must draft and display the single risk assessment document (Document Unique) and comply with the Labour Code obligations on occupational health, prevention and the use of personal protective equipment on client substation sites.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE); the national business formalities portal is the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the INPI Guichet unique. Following registration, the Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (INSEE) assigns the entity a SIREN and establishment-specific SIRET; the SIREN is the principal domestic tax identifier. The company establishes its professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr and contacts its competent SIE for corporate tax and VAT administration. A foreign entity making taxable supplies in France must register with the DGFiP service competent for foreign businesses, provide incorporation, identity, activity, and transaction evidence, and appoint a French VAT fiscal representative where required. Non-EU businesses are generally required to appoint a representative jointly liable for VAT, subject to applicable legal exceptions and mutual-assistance arrangements. An intra-Community VAT number is requested from the competent tax office; the French format is FR followed by a two-character key and the SIREN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A qualifying newly created company may elect, subject to statutory ownership, activity, size, and age conditions, for temporary partnership-style income taxation for up to five fiscal years under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code. This is a limited statutory election, not a general check-the-box regime. No general hybrid-mismatch classification election is available. Eligible companies may separately elect for a French VAT group subject to statutory conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France does not provide a general turnover threshold below which a business making taxable domestic supplies is exempt from VAT registration. The franchise en base is a small-business exemption, not a general registration threshold: the principal thresholds are EUR 85,000 for sales of goods and accommodation and EUR 37,500 for services, with respective tolerance thresholds of EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250. Applicable thresholds and eligibility should be confirmed for the relevant tax year and activity. A business that waives or is ineligible for the franchise, or that carries out transactions requiring registration, must register as applicable. For specified cross-border EU distance sales and electronic services, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold may apply under its conditions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing domestic B2B e-invoicing and transaction/payment e-reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all in-scope businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; issuance obligations begin on that date for large and mid-sized businesses and generally on 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. In-scope invoices are to be exchanged through an approved private platform (plateforme agréée), with required invoice data transmitted to the tax administration; e-reporting applies to specified transactions outside the domestic e-invoicing mandate. France does not generally require real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping of each invoice. Public-sector invoicing is subject to the separate Chorus Pro system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may be exempt with the right to deduct input VAT, subject to the applicable French VAT rules and evidence that the goods physically left the EU. Intra-Community supplies may be exempt with deduction where substantive conditions are met, including valid customer VAT identification and proof of transport. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: their place of supply is determined under the applicable B2B or B2C rules; services supplied to a business established outside the EU are generally outside French VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule, subject to exceptions and evidence of customer status and location.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and evidence of exit from the European Union, such as the customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic customs record
Commercial invoice, sales contract or purchase order, and records identifying the goods and transaction
Transport evidence appropriate to the shipment, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, or carrier delivery documentation
For intra-Community supplies, customer VAT-number verification and evidence of dispatch or transport to another Member State
For services treated as supplied outside France, contract, customer business-status evidence, and records supporting the place-of-supply treatment
Bank and payment records supporting the transaction where relevant; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory export-VAT requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The taxpayer must retain reliable evidence supporting the export or other exemption and its VAT returns. Unsupported exemption may be denied, with output VAT assessed retrospectively, applicable late-payment interest, and tax penalties. Deliberate breaches may attract increased penalties under the French Tax Code, including penalties of 40% for deliberate failure and 80% in specified cases of fraud or abusive conduct. Criminal sanctions may apply to qualifying tax fraud. France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; prudential and payment-services supervision is principally conducted by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, and customs cash-reporting matters are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has full current-account convertibility and generally unrestricted capital-account convertibility under European Union law. A French SAS may receive foreign capital, pay foreign suppliers, repay intercompany debt, distribute dividends, and remit liquidation proceeds without a general foreign-exchange approval or forced conversion requirement. Dividend and interest payments remain subject to French corporate-law approvals, withholding-tax rules, treaty or European Union relief conditions, beneficial-ownership requirements, transfer-pricing rules, anti-abuse provisions, sanctions screening, and sufficient distributable reserves. Foreign investment screening may apply to non-European Union acquisitions or control investments in activities affecting essential infrastructure, energy, national security, or other protected sectors. SCADA and substation automation activities should be screened on a transaction-specific basis before a change of control or qualifying investment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a bank, convert them into euros, or convert a prescribed percentage of receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to ordinary accounting, tax, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, and payment-service controls. There is no general statutory repatriation deadline or mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters must nevertheless comply with customs declaration requirements, maintain commercial and transport records, reconcile receivables under accounting and tax rules, and satisfy any documentary requirements imposed by banks, insurers, lenders, or trade-finance providers. Cash or equivalent monetary instruments transported into or out of the European Union at an aggregate value of EUR 10,000 or more require the applicable customs declaration. Banks may request payment-purpose, contract, invoice, export-declaration, and beneficial-owner information.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
BPCE group, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Épargne institutions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operating payments and foreign-currency collections, but low to medium as a substitute for a French domestic bank in the incorporation phase or for complex trade finance. A regulated European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, SEPA services, foreign-exchange execution, cards, and cross-border transfers, subject to its license scope, safeguarding model, onboarding policy, and correspondent access. An electronic-money account is not necessarily a bank deposit and generally does not provide a French capital-deposit certificate for SAS incorporation unless the provider is legally authorized and accepted for that purpose. Offshore or non-European Union digital EMIs may face correspondent, licensing, sanctions, data, safeguarding, and French establishment-risk limitations. The company should retain a regulated French or European bank for capital escrow, credit facilities, payroll continuity, and trade-finance capacity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal physical-appearance requirement for directors to open a corporate bank account. Remote onboarding may be permitted after electronic identification and verification, but each bank may require a video interview, certified identity documents, apostilled or legalized corporate documents, specimen signatures, a French registered office, a French telephone number, proof of operating activity, or an in-person meeting. A capital escrow account for a newly formed SAS is commonly opened subject to enhanced verification of the founders, subscribers, beneficial owners, source of funds, draft constitutional documents, and planned activity. Banks may require a director or authorized signatory to attend physically where non-resident ownership, complex ownership, high-risk countries, critical-infrastructure activity, or document-verification concerns exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent ownership chain, unidentified ultimate beneficial owner, nominee shareholder, trust arrangement, or ownership through opaque jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current extract from the French commercial register or incorporation file; executed articles of association; complete ownership chart to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and residential-address evidence for directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners; beneficial-owner declaration; shareholder register; board or shareholder resolutions; and certified translations where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, unusually large initial funding, unexplained intercompany loan, or payment from an account unrelated to the subscriber.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements; audited financial statements; tax returns or tax assessments; sale or financing agreements; loan agreements; board approvals; capital-subscription documents; investor funds-flow chart; source-of-wealth statement; proof of originating-account ownership; and written explanation linking each remittance to the capital increase or approved shareholder loan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCADA, substation, industrial-control, energy, or critical-infrastructure activity generating sanctions, export-control, dual-use, or national-security concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; customer and supplier list; product and software classification; end-use and end-user statements; geographic activity map; sanctions and export-control screening records; compliance policy; project contracts; licenses or regulatory correspondence where applicable; cybersecurity controls; and confirmation that no restricted party, embargoed destination, or prohibited end use is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or shareholder, recently incorporated entity, no operating history, no employees, virtual office, or mismatch between declared activity and expected transaction volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office agreement; premises evidence; employment or contractor plan; management biographies; signed customer and supplier contracts; quotations and invoices; projected twelve-month cash-flow statement; expected countries, currencies, volumes, and counterparties; tax registrations; insurance evidence; and explanation of the operational rationale for the French SAS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk country exposure, sanctioned counterparty, politically exposed person, adverse media, or unexplained third-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due-diligence report; sanctions-screening results; PEP declarations; independent corporate-register extracts; counterparty ownership documents; transaction-purpose memorandum; end-user certificates; legal opinions where appropriate; compliance approval record; and controls prohibiting cash, anonymous, or unrelated third-party settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for large cash withdrawals, personal-account settlement, crypto-asset flows, payment splitting, or rapid pass-through activity inconsistent with a SCADA integration contractor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; approved payment matrix; segregation-of-duties controls; supplier master-file controls; bank-account verification procedure; expected-payment profile; anti-fraud controls; written prohibition on personal-account and unapproved crypto settlement; and documented commercial invoices, purchase orders, delivery evidence, and acceptance certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, VAT, permanent-establishment, or transfer-pricing inconsistencies involving foreign shareholders or related companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax-residency certificates; VAT registration evidence; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; functional analysis; service and royalty agreements; pricing support; withholding-tax analysis; group organization chart; and confirmation of the entity's management, contracting, and accounting location.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscribed equity through a bank account held in the name of the subscriber or clearly documented investor to the French SAS capital-escrow account. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments where available and SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-euro currencies. Include an unambiguous remittance description such as 'capital contribution', 'subscription for share capital', or 'shareholder loan', together with the entity name and corporate reference. Do not combine equity, loan, service fees, or customer receipts in one unexplained transfer. Provide the bank with the subscription agreement, draft or amended articles, shareholder resolution, investor ownership and source-of-funds evidence, originating-account proof, and foreign-investment-screening analysis where relevant. The depositary bank issues the capital-deposit certificate after verification; funds are released after evidence of incorporation and registration, typically including the Kbis extract. For a later capital increase, obtain the applicable corporate approvals and updated depositary documentation before remittance. Reconcile each receipt to the general ledger and preserve bank and corporate records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro-area suppliers, subject to bank limits and fraud controls. Use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly represented by MT103 in legacy messaging or the corresponding ISO 20022 payment message, for non-SEPA currencies and jurisdictions. Include the beneficiary's legal name, verified bank-account details, invoice number, contract reference, currency, and payment purpose. For higher-value, documentary, or jurisdictionally sensitive transactions, use a commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a bank under UCP 600, with documentary presentation through the banking chain; use documentary collections under URC 522 where commercially appropriate. Apply sanctions, export-control, dual-use, end-user, and goods-classification checks before release. Match purchase orders, invoices, transport evidence, customs documentation, acceptance certificates, and payment records. Avoid third-party settlement and split payments unless documented and bank-approved. For recurring intercompany payments, use approved netting or payment-factory arrangements with arm's-length agreements and transfer-pricing support.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for identified commercial exposures, subject to bank suitability, documentation, valuation, and confirmation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency is non-deliverable or local-market restrictions make physical settlement impracticable; settlement must occur in an agreed freely convertible currency through an eligible financial institution.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management and currency conversion, with documented underlying exposure and counterparty limits.

Cross-currency swaps for longer-term financing or recurring currency exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, valuation controls, and applicable European Market Infrastructure Regulation requirements.

Plain-vanilla currency options or collars may be used for genuine commercial exposures, but speculative or leveraged structures should be prohibited under the treasury policy unless separately approved by the board and appropriately assessed under applicable financial-markets rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Dépôt des Comptes Annuels) including approval decision, management report and statutory auditor's report if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registrar of the Commercial Court) via the Guichet Unique des Entreprises / Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after fiscal year-end; shareholder approval within 6 months and filing within 1 month after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subjects the SAS and its officers to a fine of up to EUR 9,000 (EUR 45,000 for the company), court-ordered filing, and after persistent non-compliance, judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Register Update (Mise à Jour du Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs / RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique des Entreprises (RCS Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership, including direct or indirect share transfers; no separate annual confirmation is required if no change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the RBE within 30 days is punishable by an administrative fine of up to EUR 30,000 for individuals and EUR 150,000 for legal entities; continued non-compliance may trigger court enforcement

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) when, at fiscal year-end, it exceeds two of the three thresholds: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average permanent workforce exceeding 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (ANC Règlement n°2014-03) for individual statutory accounts; EU-IFRS for consolidated financial statements where legally required or authorized.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose an annual UBO confirmation declaration; the company must keep the RBE current and file any change with the Greffe within 30 days. Share transfers must be recorded in the share register and reflected in the RBE where the transfer results in a new beneficial owner or a change in holdings of 10% or more; unchanged beneficial ownership requires no annual refiling.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des Titres / Mouvements de Titres (Share and Share-Transfer Register)
Registre des Décisions et Procès-Verbaux d'Assemblées (Minute Book)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 240–EUR 960 per year (USD 260–1,050) for a registered office or domiciliation agent in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 4,000–EUR 12,000 (USD 4,400–13,200) depending on revenue, headcount and complexity; not incurred if the SAS is below the statutory audit thresholds.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. A qualifying small or medium-sized enterprise may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to the applicable ownership, turnover and capital-payment conditions; the excess remains taxable at 25%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying SMEs may benefit from the 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of profit. Research and development expenditure may qualify for the French research tax credit, generally calculated at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to statutory qualification and documentation. Other sector-specific credits, accelerated depreciation and investment incentives may apply only if their statutory conditions are satisfied.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward in principle. Utilisation is capped annually at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Unused losses may generally be carried back to the immediately preceding financial year, subject to a EUR 1 million ceiling and other statutory conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2065-SD, supported by the corporate tax schedules in the 2058-SD and 2059-SD series, filed electronically through EDI-TDFC or the company's professional account on the French tax portal. The annual accounts may also be submitted through the relevant electronic accounting filing channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly corporate income tax instalments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual return is generally due by the third working day after 1 May of the following year. For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The final corporate income tax balance is generally payable by the fifteenth day of the fourth month following the financial year-end, with a special deadline for 31 December year-ends. Instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, financial year dates, legal form, principal activity and tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS as the taxable entity. Identify foreign shareholders, foreign parent entities and any French permanent establishment or branch relationships where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base, applicable rate, amount of tax due, credits, instalments and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only profits attributable to the French SAS under French accounting and tax rules. Do not exclude French taxable income merely because ownership or financing is non-French.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or tax loss, including permanent add-backs, deductible items, tax-exempt income, non-deductible expenses and timing differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible expenses, including unsupported management charges, excessive interest, penalties and expenses lacking a business purpose. Document cross-border charges and their French benefit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, prior-year losses carried forward, losses utilised and remaining losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French annual limitation on loss utilisation and maintain schedules supporting the origin, amount and continuing availability of each loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, capital losses, applicable exemptions and special tax regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify gains on business assets, shares, intellectual property and intra-group transfers. Treaty allocation does not automatically remove French filing obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certain general expenses, including specified high-value management compensation, attendance fees and other statutory disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include relevant payments to foreign directors, parent companies and related parties where the form requires disclosure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information on subsidiaries, participations, distributions and certain related corporate transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report material foreign participations and distributions consistently with the participation exemption and withholding-tax analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research tax credit, foreign tax credits and other eligible credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only where permitted by French domestic law or an applicable tax treaty and retain foreign tax certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of transactions with associated enterprises, jurisdictions, amounts, methods and documentation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Generally required where the statutory EUR 50 million threshold or another qualifying condition is met. Reconcile all amounts with the general ledger, statutory accounts and Local File.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information relevant to the deductibility of financial charges and thin-capitalisation or earnings-stripping restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Test interest deductions under the French earnings-stripping rules, related-party debt limitations and anti-hybrid rules. Maintain debt agreements, repayment evidence and arm's-length support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: VAT CA3 and CA12, where applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Periodic or annual French VAT returns for taxable supplies, imports, reverse-charge transactions and deductible input VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SCADA integration, installation and substation automation contracts must be analysed for place-of-supply, construction or installation rules, reverse charge and fixed-establishment implications.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted corporate income tax filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, subject to statutory exceptions and escalation for formal notices or abusive conduct. Late payment generally bears late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, subject to the applicable statutory rules. Deliberate concealment, fraudulent manoeuvres or repeated non-compliance may result in an 80% tax surcharge, criminal tax-fraud prosecution and separate penalties. Failure to submit or substantiate transfer-pricing documentation can trigger a penalty generally based on the higher of the statutory minimum and a percentage of the reassessed or undocumented transactions, subject to the applicable legal provision.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident. A qualifying EU or EEA parent may obtain a domestic exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, commonly where the parent holds at least 10% for the required period and anti-abuse and subject-to-tax conditions are met. Tax treaties may reduce the rate, commonly to 5%, 10% or 15%, depending on the treaty and ownership level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The recipient should establish treaty residence and beneficial ownership before payment, provide a current tax-residence certificate issued or validated by the foreign tax authority, and satisfy the relevant ownership, holding-period, limitation-on-benefits and anti-abuse conditions. French administrative forms commonly used for treaty relief include Forms 5000 and 5001 for dividends, Form 5002 for interest and Form 5003 for royalties, as applicable. The French payer must retain the supporting documents, apply the reduced rate or exemption only where the legal conditions are met, and otherwise withhold at the domestic rate. Refund claims may be filed with the French tax administration where relief at source was not obtained.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties and similar payments to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and special rules for non-cooperative jurisdictions. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions may apply, including payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, certain anti-abuse situations and specific statutory categories. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and frequently provide a reduced royalty rate and an exemption or reduced rate for interest. The payer must separately test beneficial ownership, treaty residence, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules and the French non-cooperative-jurisdiction regime.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File obligations generally apply where the French entity or the French tax-consolidated group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or where it is controlled by, controls or belongs to a group including an entity meeting the EUR 400 million threshold. A French entity below that threshold may still be required to provide sufficient transfer-pricing evidence during an audit. An annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies at or above EUR 50 million of turnover or gross assets, or where another statutory group condition is met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a standalone regime formally equivalent to the United Arab Emirates or certain offshore Economic Substance Regulations. French substance is assessed through general anti-abuse principles, transfer-pricing rules, permanent-establishment rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, the place of effective management, anti-conduit doctrines, controlled-foreign-company rules, interest limitation rules and the general anti-abuse rule. The SAS should maintain French decision-making evidence, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises, technical capability, contract performance records, bank-account control, customer and supplier evidence, and contemporaneous support for all intercompany charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting French revenue, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, concealing cash receipts, or submitting knowingly inaccurate corporate income tax or VAT returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, a surcharge that may reach 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse, and criminal tax-fraud penalties. Individuals may face imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000; aggravated cases may reach seven years and EUR 3 million. Fines for legal persons may be increased to five times the individual fine where the statutory conditions are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may incur criminal liability, civil liability and tax-authority liability where they personally participated, authorised the conduct or committed serious and repeated management misconduct causing non-recovery of tax. Courts may impose management bans, professional disqualification, asset confiscation or a travel restriction where legally justified; travel bans are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length prices for engineering services, software, equipment, guarantees, royalties, loans or management charges; shifting SCADA project profits offshore; or failing to produce a Local File, Master File or transaction-level support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Profit adjustment, withholding-tax exposure, interest, penalties and transfer-pricing documentation penalties under the French Tax Procedure Code. The amount depends on the nature of the failure, the reassessed profits or undocumented transactions, repeated conduct and cooperation during the audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability to the company or creditors and criminal exposure if documentation failure forms part of intentional tax fraud, false accounting, misuse of corporate assets or insolvency misconduct. Ordinary pricing disagreement alone does not automatically create personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Artificial Residency or Permanent-Establishment Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal French SAS without real decision-making or operational capacity, routing contracts through France while work is performed elsewhere, or concealing a foreign permanent establishment or a French permanent establishment of a foreign enterprise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reallocation of profits, denial of treaty benefits, French corporate income tax, VAT and payroll reassessments, interest and tax surcharges. Artificial arrangements may be challenged under the French abuse-of-law or general anti-abuse framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for deliberate misrepresentation, fictitious accounting, insolvency misconduct or tax fraud. Management bans, confiscation and criminal penalties may apply after judicial proceedings; there is no automatic veil piercing solely because the company has foreign shareholders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper Dividend, Royalty or Interest Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without distributable reserves, disguising dividends as royalties or service fees, claiming treaty relief without residence or beneficial-ownership evidence, or failing to withhold and remit tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, interest, applicable surcharges, denial of treaty relief and potential sanctions for unlawful distributions or misuse of corporate assets. Civil restitution may be ordered for improperly distributed amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore unlawful distributions and may face civil or criminal liability for knowingly approving fictitious accounts, unlawful distributions, misuse of corporate assets or fraudulent withholding-tax treatment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained funds, disguising beneficial owners, processing payments inconsistent with the SCADA contracting business, failing to maintain customer or supplier due diligence, or misusing nominee shareholders and accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious-transaction reporting obligations may apply to regulated intermediaries, and money-laundering offences may lead to imprisonment of up to five years and substantial fines, with aggravated penalties in specified circumstances. Failure to register or accurately report beneficial ownership may produce administrative and criminal consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally prosecuted for laundering, complicity, concealment or false declarations. Asset freezing, confiscation, management prohibitions and judicial travel restrictions may be ordered where statutory conditions are satisfied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining false books, recording fictitious project costs, diverting company funds, paying personal expenses through the SAS, or approving contracts that are manifestly contrary to the company's interests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil damages, repayment, shareholder remedies, insolvency proceedings and criminal sanctions for misuse of corporate assets, false accounting or distribution of fictitious dividends. Additional tax reassessment and penalties may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS's limited liability does not protect directors from their own tortious or criminal conduct. Directors may face restitution, disqualification from management, personal liability for an insufficiency of assets in insolvency where serious management faults contributed to the shortfall, confiscation and imprisonment where applicable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying automation equipment, undervaluing imports, omitting installation or construction services from VAT analysis, claiming input VAT without valid invoices, or using incorrect reverse-charge treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT and customs reassessment, import duties, interest, administrative penalties, seizure and potentially criminal customs or tax proceedings. Fraudulent conduct can attract aggravated tax penalties and criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise for intentional fraud, customs smuggling, false declarations or serious management misconduct. Civil restitution and judicial restrictions may accompany criminal sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sanctions, Export-Control and Dual-Use Equipment Risk
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Supplying industrial-control, grid-automation or related technical items to sanctioned persons, prohibited territories or restricted end users without required screening, authorisation or contractual controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative measures, transaction prohibitions, asset freezes, fines, licence consequences and criminal penalties may apply under French, European Union and applicable international sanctions regimes. Penalties depend on the relevant measure and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted for intentional or negligent sanctions breaches, complicity or obstruction. Personal fines, imprisonment, confiscation and management prohibitions may apply; a travel ban requires a competent judicial or administrative basis and is not automatic.
